source: Vinokurova N. Lexical Categories and Argument Structure: A Study with Reference to Sakha. Utrecht, 2005. (LOT Dissertation Series, no. 103)
notes: The semantic classification below also depends on the attachment level of N. For example, the meaning ‘provide with N’ is more flexible than ‘use N as instrument’: in the former the noun can be plural or modified but not in the latter. Again, this is expected: although sharpness/bluntness of a knife affects its efficiency as an instrument, there are no two instruments like a sharp knife versus a blunt knife. Similarly, in (23-24) there is only one instrument – a whip, singular and unmodified. The table in (25) gives a summary indication of meanings, cognate objects and N-restrictions (whether the incorporated N can be plural and modified or must be bare).
